reporting-org.narrative: Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs

description.narrative: The UK’s £100 million Biodiverse Landscapes Fund (BLF) aims to reduce poverty, protect and restore biodiversity and lessen the impact of climate change in six environmentally critical landscapes across the globe. These are: - The Kavango-Zambezi (KAZA) Transfrontier Conservation Area, covering areas of Angola, Botswana, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe. - Mesoamerica, covering areas of Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras. - Western Congo Basin, covering areas of Cameroon, Gabon and Republic of Congo. - Andes Amazon, covering areas of Ecuador and Peru. - Lower Mekong, covering areas of Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam. - Madagascar. The BLF has 3 core aims: - people: to develop economic opportunities through investment in nature in support of climate adaptation and resilience and poverty reduction. - nature: to slow, halt or reverse biodiversity loss in globally significant regions for biodiversity. - climate: to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and safeguard natural carbon sinks. It will meet these aims by: - reducing poverty and creating sustainable economic development for communities living in, and dependent upon, environmentally precious landscapes. - protecting and restoring ecosystems and biologically diverse landscapes helping to mitigate climate change by preserving carbon sinks and ecosystems. - addressing the causes of environmental degradation. - supporting national and local governments, park authorities and communities to achieve long-term sustainable management and use of natural resources Funding will be distributed across the landscapes according to demands and needs.

title.narrative: Biodiverse Landscapes Fund Lower Mekong Full Business Case

description.narrative: The Business Case summarises the results of the detailed programme design process; describes the nature of the programme, including its intended outcomes and impact, appraises the evidence for what interventions will be delivered and how it will be delivered; explains clearly and succinctly what the programme will do, in what timeframe and is explicit about risks and uncertainties and how they will be managed, including by partners in delivery chains and departmental oversight; records an understanding for relevant departments including Defra, our partners and intended beneficiaries about what we are planning to do and the results we expect to achieve, and how they will be assessed.

title.narrative: Biodiverse Landscapes Fund: Andes Amazon Grant Funding Agreement

description.narrative: The Grant Funding Agreement governing each BLF programme is an agreement between the Lead Delivery Partner and Defra, signed by the BLF Fund Manager as a contractor for Defra. It outlines the terms and conditions of a grant, to ensure it is used for its intended purpose and that the funding body can monitor the project's activity and expenditure.
